direction: D2 Who carries the fashion: communal vs generational change (WP6)

hypotheses.statement: Communal dominance: within-stayer share rho >= 0.70 (last list position) and >= 0.60 (any role), E = 2022-23 -> L = 2025-26, profile keys.
Generational increment at first list position: rho_first lower than rho_last by >= 0.2; entrant first-position keys' L NAME share exceeds stayers'.

Not driven by entrant co-authors: (i) on stayers' author-paper rows with key FE, the implied E->L change at share_new_coauthors = 0 is >= 0.5 x the population change; (ii) teams whose keys all appeared earlier (rolling) rise by >= 0.5 x the population rise.

Style vs topic channel: across markers, within-stayer change regressed on population change has slope ~1 (falsified if < 0.7); the generational increment share 1 - within/pop is larger for style than for topic markers.
Pre-LLM replication: with email keys, 2018 -> 2020, the NAME and colon (compound) rise is >= 50% within stayers (any role primary).

S2_1.statement: Even among retitled resubmissions (destination >= 2024), NAME is not added on net, against the population drift implied by the pairs' years.
S2_1.caveat: Pairs are selected on retitling (the export keeps one submission per family); transition rates are not behaviour.

S2_2.statement: Future-tie placebo: past-collaborator exposure is no larger than future-collaborator exposure in the clean sample (homophily, not tie contagion).
